claims.statement: The Codex hook reduces a submitted prompt to a bounded recall query: a prompt within 8192 characters and 8192 UTF-8 bytes is used trimmed, while a longer prompt keeps its tail, cut by character and then by UTF-8 byte without splitting a character.
PrepareContextRequest requires a query of 1 to 8192 characters containing non-whitespace text, and max_bytes defaults to 8000 within a permitted range of 512 to 32768.

The Codex hook calls POST /v1/context/prepare with max_bytes 8000, adds include_code, assembly, or bootstrap_receipt_id only when configured, and never requests include_receipt, so automatic recall receives the four-field envelope.

The HTTP prepare route converts the transport request by dropping scope_id from the body, which selects the Scope, and when access control is configured it requires read permission on the target Scope and every referenced Scope before preparing.

ScopedContextApplication.prepare returns an empty result without recall when assembly is present with an empty sections list and neither include_code nor include_reuse is set, attaching a receipt only when include_receipt is set.
Reuse across referenced Scopes is unsupported: include_reuse fails with context-reuse-cross-scope-unsupported when the Scope has context references.

Without an assembly, preparation recalls Memory, Experience, and Topic Memory; with an assembly it recalls only the families its sections name. Round zero requests Memory up to the builder's 16-candidate ceiling, Experience up to 8, and Topic Memory up to 8.

Each preparation shares one query-embedding wait budget, whose default recall_embedding_timeout_seconds is 0.5 seconds and whose configured maximum is 60 seconds; only the time spent waiting on embeddings is charged to it.

Embedding degradation is folded into one preparation reason in which inference_timeout outranks inference_unavailable; in auto mode, when the embedding times out or is unavailable and FTS is available, Atomic Memory search falls back to text retrieval instead of failing.

The recall-sufficiency gate is a pure, model-free verdict that checks, in order, no-content, budget-floor, rerank-enabled, thin-candidates, thin-families, weak-top-1, weak-lexical, and then sufficient.

The gate policy is disabled by default; when enabled, it allows at most recall_gate_max_rounds expansion rounds (default 2, capped at 2) and uses default thresholds of 2 minimum candidates, 0.35 top score, 0.02 top gap, and 0.5 lexical overlap.
Expansion rounds change only the admission floor: round 1 uses a semantic floor of 0.15 and round 2 uses 0.10, and a SearchPlan never sets a limit, search mode, or rerank candidate bound.

The expansion loop runs while the verdict is insufficient, families remain recoverable, and expansions are below the cap; when still insufficient at the cap, a non-weak-top-1 verdict becomes at-max-rounds, and any error keeps the last committed candidates, records expansion-failed, and lets the preparation succeed.

Before the round-zero assessment and before each expansion-round assessment, the Runtime runs a budget probe that reuses the builder's own selection code and reports delivered, truncated, and dropped items plus unused bytes. The gate's budget-floor verdict uses budget_bounded, which is size-dependent: at the 512-byte floor, any dropped or truncated item or delivered content that used all headroom is budget-bound; above the floor, budget-bound requires exhausted headroom together with a dropped or truncated item, so fitting pressure alone is not sufficient for every budget. The budget-floor check runs only after the no-content check.
The builder raises PreparedContextInvariantError when accumulated candidate lists exceed their family ceilings, which are a guard after the recall loop has already applied those ceilings.

On the default path the builder interleaves Memory, Topic Memory, and Experience, keeps at most 8 entries and 2 Experience entries, caps each body at 2000 bytes, and raises an output-budget invariant when the rendered content exceeds max_bytes.

Entries that do not fit whole are shortened to the longest prefix that fits, with a 64-byte minimum: on the default path a source shorter than 64 bytes that does not fit whole is dropped as below-min-bytes and an entry with no truncation of at least 64 bytes that fits is dropped as no-fitting-truncation; on the assembly path a longest fitting prefix under 64 bytes is dropped as below-min-bytes.

The PreparedContext envelope has schema, status, content, and content_bytes, with an empty context requiring null content and zero bytes, and a ready context requiring non-blank content whose UTF-8 length equals content_bytes; the Codex hook validates this shape and rejects content above 8000 bytes.
A receipt is attached only when include_receipt is set; if the receipt is incomplete or its serialized form exceeds 8192 bytes, the transport layer drops it and returns the four-field envelope.

With include_reuse the response becomes PreparedContextWithReuse, and the reuse binding attaches to the final selected origins and their observed lifecycle versions rather than to every recalled candidate.

Errors raised during recall propagate out of preparation: an Atomic Memory search exception is re-raised after recording a failed search, and the HTTP layer maps inference timeouts and unavailability to 503 with codes inference_timeout and inference_unavailable, while unmapped exceptions become 500 internal_error.

The Codex hook fails open: an HTTP 503 or a timeout or socket error records server_unavailable, a 401 records authentication_failed, a 404 without an error code records version_mismatch, other unexpected responses or invalid envelopes record invalid_response, and an empty response emits an empty event; none of these inject context.

Topic Memory reuses the Memory query vector when both use the same embedding model and the query fits Topic search limits; otherwise it embeds its own query, and it falls back to FTS when the shared embedding budget is exhausted.

Before the Runtime assembles context, the route fills each plugin assembly section from the plugin's search_artifacts call; a plugin error below status 500 is re-raised, while a status 500 or higher leaves that section empty and marks it search_failed so the receipt records the failed search.

A ContextAssembly accepts at most 4 sections with unique families, each limit from 1 to 8; when assembly is supplied without sections it defaults to a memory section with limit 6 and an experience section with limit 2, and an experience section cannot exceed 2 entries.

A prepare request whose assembly section limits sum above context_assembly_max_entries (default 8) is rejected with context-assembly-entry-limit before any recall, and the HTTP layer maps InvalidRuntimeRequestError to 422 invalid_request.

When bootstrap_receipt_id is supplied and a bootstrap receipt store is configured, Memory identities already injected for that receipt are excluded from round zero and the Memory search limit grows by the number excluded for that Scope, so session-start Memory is not returned twice.
Code context is fetched only when include_code is set, and a CodeError from the code query records a failed code search and contributes no code candidates without failing the preparation.

When no selected family yields a candidate, the gate reports no-content as sufficient and the builder returns an empty context, so the route responds with status empty, content null, and content_bytes 0 rather than an error.

The PreparedContextReceipt carries schema, receipt_id, policy_id, query_digest, content_digest, requested_max_bytes, used_bytes, truncated, non_deterministic, retrieval, selected, omitted, and stages, recording digests of the query and content rather than their text; if receipt assembly raises, the Runtime logs context.receipt.omitted and returns the context without a receipt.

prepare_reuse seals a reuse binding that carries the content digest, content_bytes, ordered roots, the Memory dependency snapshot, cited code file digests, expires_at, and trust historical-data, valid for 5 minutes; it rejects origins from another Scope or from a family other than atomic-memory, and fails if the dependency snapshot is over the limit or cited code has changed.

validate_reuse re-reads the Memory dependency snapshot and cited code digests without recall or model calls; a binding for another scope or identity is rejected as invalid, and a changed snapshot or changed cited file raises context-reuse-source-changed.

The POST /v1/context/check route authorizes SCOPE_READ on the target Scope for the check, and the x-powercontext-resolve-target header is honored only for a service principal with access control configured on a before_send phase, requiring GATEWAY_INVOKE, otherwise it raises AccessDeniedError.

check_context rejects bodies above the phase limit or 1 MiB with ContextCheckTooLargeError (HTTP 413 context_payload_too_large), withholds unconfigured target profiles with target_unsupported, returns the privacy policy's block or withhold decision with its reason codes when the policy is enforcing and the assessment is not allow or is incomplete, and otherwise returns allow.

For before_send, every prepared_contexts location must hold bytes whose length and SHA-256 match the verified reuse binding with trust historical-data, and any binding or reuse failure withholds the check with context-refresh-required; a profile that requires prepared contexts with none supplied fails with context-binding-required.

For before_release the check opens the request binding sealed at send time and requires matching identity, scope, target profile, policy fingerprint, and phase, then re-validates every retained prepared binding; any mismatch withholds with context-refresh-required.

An allowed check seals a binding valid for 60 seconds, capped by the earliest reuse expiry, with a 300-second correlation window for before_send; if sealing exceeds capacity the check withholds with binding-capacity-exceeded.
